title: [finding] `MasterDetailForm` keys a declined detail section on `undefined-<index>` — no collision (the index saves it), but the entry has no identity across reorder
body:
Found while implementing #6360 (the render half of the #5940 decline). Out of scope there by name — that card's dispatch order listed this line as "file, do not fix".

## The claim, and the measured correction

The #6360 dispatch order described `MasterDetailForm.tsx:240` as a key that *"collapses to `undefined-0` for declined details"*, implying a duplicate-key collision. **That half is not true, and the correction matters more than the finding:**

```tsx
{details.map((d, i) => (
  <section key={`${d.childObject}-${i}`} className="space-y-2">
```

`i` is the map index, so it is unique among siblings by construction. Two declined details produce `undefined-0` and `undefined-1` — distinct. There is **no** duplicate-key warning and no remount collision. Anyone acting on the collision reading would be chasing something that does not happen.

## What IS true

For a detail whose `childObject` never resolved (the #5940 decline path), the key degrades to an **index-only key wearing a literal `undefined-` prefix**. The data half contributes nothing, so the section's React identity is its *position* in `details`.

That is the classic index-key hazard, and it is not academic here because the sibling row-state array is indexed the same way:

```tsx
// MasterDetailForm.tsx — one row-state per detail collection
const [state, setState] = useState<RowState[]>(() => rawDetails.map(() => ({ rows: [], original: [] })));
...
value={state[i]?.rows ?? []}
```

Remove or reorder a detail entry above a declined one and both the DOM node and `state[i]` re-associate with a different collection — the failure mode index keys exist to warn about. For a *resolved* detail the same expression is `childObject`-qualified and mostly escapes this; the declined entry is the one with no identity at all.

## Why it is filed rather than fixed

There is no obvious stable identity for a detail entry that carries no `childObject` — that is precisely what the decline establishes. Picking one (authored order? a synthesized id? refusing to render the entry?) is a design call, not a mechanical fix, so it does not belong as a rider on #6360's render-branch change.

## Class

Same family as #5940 / #6188 / #6194 / #6360 — an unresolved optional sub-key reaching a read unguarded. This is the *identity* read rather than the fetch or render read.

Filed unassigned for triage. Severity is a triage call: nothing is user-visible today unless details are reordered or removed.
